run.question: What is the current state of the checkout deployment in the otel-demo namespace: desired versus available replicas, restart counts of its pods, and any recent events for it?

report.summary: The checkout Deployment in otel-demo is at its desired scale and fully ready: spec.replicas 1, status.replicas 1, availableReplicas 1, readyReplicas 1, updatedReplicas 1, terminatingReplicas 0, unavailableReplicas null, Available=True (MinimumReplicasAvailable) and Progressing=True (NewReplicaSetAvailable). Its single pod checkout-6578865d87-v6flf (owner ReplicaSet checkout-6578865d87, pod startTime 2026-11-23T14:36:30Z, container started 14:37:11Z) is Running, ready true, restartCount 0, lastState empty. All 7 events touching checkout objects in the authorized window are Normal and describe a fresh start (ScalingReplicaSet 0->1, SuccessfulCreate, Scheduled, Pulling, Pulled, Created, Started) between 14:36:30Z and 14:37:11Z; no eviction, OOM, killing, backoff or probe-failure event names checkout. The Deployment itself was created inside the window (creationTimestamp 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z, generation 1, helm Apply at 14:36:29Z), and namespace-wide events show 25 otel-demo Deployment ScalingReplicaSet and 23 ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate events at the same time, i.e. a namespace-wide rollout rather than a checkout fault. The read application log lines show successful order flow (PlaceOrder, payment went through, confirmation email) through 15:13:00Z. Prometheus was unreachable in this Run, so kube-state-metrics time series for replica availability and restart counters could not be read, and the error-keyword log query returned no_data rather than a citable zero. No fault or root cause was identified; root_cause is null.

The checkout Deployment appearing at 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z (generation 1, helm Apply) is most consistent with a namespace-wide rollout or fresh install of the otel-demo stack around 14:36-14:38 rather than a checkout failure; this stays a hypothesis because the change_history integration is not available to confirm what triggered the deployment.

Trace data from Jaeger (checkout error spans or error rates) was not queried, so request-level error rates for checkout remain unchecked.
